# Summary of Political Manifesto 2024

## Economic Policy

The manifesto emphasises economic stability following recent global challenges, including the pandemic and international conflicts. Key economic commitments include:

- Reducing employee National Insurance from 12% to 6% by April 2027
- Abolishing the main rate of self-employed National Insurance by the end of the Parliament
- Introducing a "Triple Lock Plus" for pensioners, ensuring both State Pension and tax-free allowances rise with inflation, earnings, or 2.5%
- Expanding free childcare to 30 hours weekly for children from nine months old
- Reforming Child Benefit to a household-based system with a £120,000 threshold
- Maintaining fiscal rules requiring public sector debt to fall and borrowing below 3% of GDP

## Immigration and Border Security

The document proposes significant immigration reforms:

- Introducing a legally binding annual cap on migration
- Continuing deportation programmes for illegal migrants
- Reforming international asylum treaties
- Increasing visa fees and health surcharges for migrants
- Implementing health checks for incoming migrants

## Defence and National Security

Defence spending commitments include:

- Increasing defence spending to 2.5% of GDP by 2030
- Investing £10 billion in munitions production
- Continuing support for Ukraine
- Developing a National Defence and Resilience Plan

## Public Services

Healthcare proposals include:

- Increasing NHS spending above inflation annually
- Recruiting 92,000 additional nurses and 28,000 doctors
- Expanding pharmacy services and community diagnostic centres
- Implementing NHS productivity improvements through technology

## Housing and Infrastructure

The manifesto commits to:

- Building 1.6 million homes during the Parliament
- Abolishing Stamp Duty for first-time buyers on homes up to £425,000
- Investing £36 billion in transport from redirected funds
- Protecting Green Belt while enabling brownfield development

## Energy and Environment

Environmental commitments include:

- Maintaining net zero by 2050 target
- Tripling offshore wind capacity
- Supporting nuclear power expansion
- Continuing annual oil and gas licensing rounds
- Introducing carbon pricing mechanisms for imports
